probes.summary: Read-only router, host-routing, Kubernetes membership, and LAN-path checks completed.
Per-node HTTP pods passed direct cross-LAN HTTP, ClusterIP HTTP, DNS, and targeted flannel VXLAN traversal checks; evaluator state was removed.
limitations: crictl was unavailable on node3 and node4, so local runtime cleanup confirmation relied on cluster-wide namespace/object deletion confirmed from node2.

probes.summary: Read-only operational audits completed across all nodes and the cluster API.

assertions.summary: VyOS owns both LAN gateways; node2 is the Ready control plane and node3/node4 are Ready workers with LAN InternalIPs, routed LAN paths, a LAN API endpoint, and flannel pod routes.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show; sudo -n grep -E '10\.10\.(1|2)\.254' /config/config.boot; sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.eth1.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.eth2.forwarding; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show ip route
evidence.observation: eth1=10.10.1.254/24 and eth2=10.10.2.254/24; saved config contains both addresses; both LANs are directly connected; IPv4 forwarding and both interface forwarding settings are 1.

evidence.command: sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get nodes -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'; ip route show; ip route get 10.10.2.254; sudo -n grep -H -E -- '--node-ip|server:' /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf; sudo -n ss -tnp | grep -E '(:6443|:10250)'
evidence.observation: kubectl reported node2 Ready/control-plane at 10.10.1.10, node3 Ready at 10.10.2.10, and node4 Ready at 10.10.2.11; API endpoint was https://10.10.1.10:6443; node2 routes 10.10.2.0/24 via 10.10.1.254; flannel routes 10.244.1.0/24 and 10.244.2.0/24 via flannel.1; kubelet uses the LAN API endpoint.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show; ip route get 10.10.1.10; sudo -n grep -H -E -- '--node-ip|server:' /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf; sudo -n ss -tnp | grep -E '(:6443|:10250)'
evidence.observation: node3 has LAN address 10.10.2.10/24; route to 10.10.1.10 uses 10.10.2.254; kubelet configuration points to https://10.10.1.10:6443; kubelet and kube-proxy have established connections from 10.10.2.10 to the LAN API.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show; ip route get 10.10.1.10; sudo -n grep -H -E -- '--node-ip|server:' /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf; sudo -n ss -tnp | grep -E '(:6443|:10250)'
evidence.observation: node4 has LAN address 10.10.2.11/24; route to 10.10.1.10 uses 10.10.2.254; kubelet configuration points to https://10.10.1.10:6443; kubelet and kube-proxy have established connections from 10.10.2.11 to the LAN API.

limitations: The authored plan did not authorize a reboot, so post-reboot behavior was not directly exercised; persistence-related configuration and enabled services were inspected.

assertions.summary: Evaluator pods were placed one per Kubernetes node, communicated directly across both LANs, accessed the ClusterIP service and service DNS, and generated HTTP-bearing flannel VXLAN traffic through node1.

evidence.command: sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy get pods -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy get service eval-http -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy get endpoints eval-http -o wide
evidence.observation: eval-http pods were Running on node2 10.244.0.6, node3 10.244.1.3, and node4 10.244.2.3; service ClusterIP was 10.107.67.213; endpoints contained all three pod IPs.

evidence.command: sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy exec eval-client -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.1.3:8080; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy exec eval-client -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.244.2.3:8080; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy exec eval-client -- nslookup eval-http.eval-routed-ot3qzsy.svc.cluster.local; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n eval-routed-ot3qzsy exec eval-client -- wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.107.67.213:8080
evidence.observation: Direct requests from the node2 client returned HTTP content from both node3 and node4 pods; 40 repeated cross-LAN direct requests succeeded with 0 failures; DNS resolved the service to 10.107.67.213; ClusterIP requests returned successful HTTP responses from node2, node3, and node4 endpoints.

evidence.command: tcpdump -i eth1 -nn -c 20 "udp port 8472 and host 10.10.1.10 and (host 10.10.2.10 or host 10.10.2.11)"; tcpdump -i eth2 -nn -c 20 "udp port 8472 and host 10.10.1.10 and (host 10.10.2.10 or host 10.10.2.11)"
evidence.observation: Both eth1 and eth2 captures recorded flannel VXLAN/8472 traffic: 10.10.1.10 exchanged encapsulated packets with 10.10.2.10 carrying 10.244.0.5↔10.244.1.3 HTTP 200 traffic, and with 10.10.2.11 carrying 10.244.0.5↔10.244.2.3 HTTP 200 traffic; each capture reported 0 dropped packets.

limitations: crictl was unavailable on node3 and node4 during cleanup confirmation, but node2 confirmed namespace, pods, service, and endpoints absent and node1 confirmed all evaluator capture files absent.

assertions.summary: All audited nodes had no active failed services, duplicate Kubernetes/CNI/runtime stacks, enabled SSH, conflicting route/firewall/NAT state, debug residue, or evaluator residue. Required Kubernetes, flannel, runtime, certificate, manifest, route, and saved VyOS state was coherent; current system pods were Running/Ready.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; systemctl is-enabled ssh sshd; ip route show; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat source rules; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat destination rules; sudo -n stat -c '%A %U %s %y %n' /config/config.boot; sudo -n find /tmp /var/tmp /config /home /root -xdev -maxdepth 3 ...
evidence.observation: No failed services; SSH disabled/inactive; only expected connected/default routes; VyOS reported NAT not configured; saved /config/config.boot exists; no suspicious or evaluator-residue names were found.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; dpkg-query -W -f='${binary:Package}\t${Version}\n'; systemctl list-unit-files --type=service; ps -eo user,pid,comm; systemctl is-enabled ssh sshd; ip route show; sudo -n nft list ruleset; sudo -n find /etc/kubernetes /etc/cni/net.d /var/lib/kubelet -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%M %u %p\n'
evidence.observation: No failed services; one coherent containerd/kubeadm/kubectl/kubelet/kubernetes-cni package set; expected containerd, kubelet, kube-proxy, flanneld, and control-plane processes; SSH disabled/not found/inactive; routes and KUBE/FLANNEL chains matched the active cluster; required protected Kubernetes/CNI paths were present. Root-owned kubeadm/flannel setup manifests and root kubeconfig were classified as coherent active-cluster artifacts, not abandoned residue.

evidence.observation: No failed services; same single coherent Kubernetes/containerd/CNI package set as node2; expected kubelet, kube-proxy, flanneld, and containerd processes; SSH disabled/not found/inactive; expected LAN, flannel, kube-proxy, and flannel NAT state; no suspicious, debug, credential-copy, installer, backup, or evaluator names beyond the required flannel binary.

evidence.command: sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get nodes -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get pods -A -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get daemonsets,deployments,statefulsets,jobs,cronjobs -A; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get services,endpoints -A -o wide; sudo -n -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get namespace eval-routed-ot3qzsy; sudo -n stat -c '%A %U %s %y %n' /root/kubeadm-init.yaml /root/kube-flannel.yml /root/.kube /root/.kube/config

actions_performed: Created evaluator namespace eval-routed-ot3qzsy with a busybox HTTP DaemonSet, ClusterIP service, and node2 client pod.
Collected node1 eth1/eth2 captures during repeated cross-LAN pod requests.
Deleted the evaluator namespace and confirmed its Kubernetes objects absent.
Removed evaluator capture files and confirmed evaluator capture processes/files absent.
Closed managed live evidence exactly once after all probes and cleanup.
overall_summary: All three authored assertions passed independently. The routed Kubernetes cluster is currently healthy and clean; live evidence collection is closed.
